title_zh: André Perold（HighVista Strategies）：学者型投资人（复播 EP.02）
subtitle_zh: 从哈佛课堂到 HighVista：André Perold 谈风险本位的配置与主动投资之道。
summary_zh: 本期 Capital Allocators 是一集复播（replay），Ted Seides 对话 HighVista Strategies 首席投资官兼联席管理合伙人 André Perold——他执掌一只规模约 30 亿美元、采用类捐赠基金（endowment-like）多资产方式、强调广泛分散与风险管理的基金。Perold 曾在 Harvard Business School 任教逾 30 年，是荣休的 George Gund 金融与银行学教授、案例教学（case method）的传奇大师，发表 27 篇期刊论文、两本书与上百篇案例，几乎以课堂逐字记录了现代金融的演进——从 Black-Scholes 定价、RJR Nabisco 杠杆收购、Bankers Trust 衍生品、长期资本管理公司（LTCM）到危机前的杠杆贷款。核心是他学者型投资人的方法论：关于优势（edge），他直言大多数人任何时候都没有优势，关键是知道自己何时拥有、何时没有，并在拥有时善加利用；关于主动管理与费用，他认为低费用高 alpha 是个误称，因为真正稀缺的人才昂贵，费后回报才是衡量起点。他还谈到生物科技特许权使用费、小盘银行、小盘股东行动主义等冷门角落，以及资产配置驱动回报与识人之难。结尾的人生快问快答里，他给出永不退休、往大处想、经营人脉、为自己制造运气、审慎冒险的忠告。

turns.en: My guest on today's show is Andre Perold. For those who know Andre, he needs no introduction. Andre is the chief investment officer and co-managing partner at Hivis to Strategies, where for the last dozen years he has sat at the helm of an now $3 billion fund that takes a multi-asset class endowment-like approach, emphasizing broad diversification and risk management.
turns.zh: 今天的嘉宾是 André Perold。认识 André 的人不需要我再介绍。André 是 HighVista Strategies 的首席投资官兼联席管理合伙人，过去十多年里，他一直执掌着一只如今规模 30 亿美元的基金，采用类似捐赠基金的多资产类别方式，强调广泛分散和风险管理。

turns.en: Over this period, Andre has definitively rebuffed the cliche that those who can't do teach. You see, in his prior career, he spent over 30 years teaching at the Harvard Business School, where he is the George Gund Professor of Finance and Banking Emeritus.
turns.zh: 在这段时间里，André 彻底驳斥了那句老话——无能者才去教书。在他此前的职业生涯中，他在哈佛商学院任教超过 30 年，是荣休的 George Gund 金融与银行学教授。

turns.en: Andre had a distinguished career teaching investment management at Harvard and is a legendary master of the case study classroom. Just about everyone in the investment profession, with Harvard Business School on the resume, once took a seat in his classroom.
turns.zh: André 在哈佛教授投资管理的职业生涯卓著非凡，是案例教学课堂的传奇大师。几乎每一位投资行业从业者，只要简历上有哈佛商学院，都曾坐在他的课堂里。

turns.en: Andre received numerous awards for teaching excellence, including being voted the school's most outstanding professor in a Business Week student survey.
turns.zh: André 获得过众多教学卓越奖项，包括在《Business Week》学生评选中被票选为学校最杰出的教授。

turns.en: While at Harvard, Andre authored and co-authored 27 articles in financial journals, two books, and over 100 case studies, all relating to investment management, capital markets, and the financial system.
turns.zh: 在哈佛期间，André 独立或合作撰写了 27 篇金融期刊文章、两本书，以及超过 100 篇案例研究，全部涉及投资管理、资本市场和金融体系。

turns.en: He literally chronicled the development of modern finance as it occurred through his work at Harvard Business School. To give you a sense, some of my favorites among his collection of case studies includes, in 1994, Black Scholes Pricing for the HP-12C Calculator, in 1990, the RJR Nabisco, LBO, in 1994, Bankers Trust Derivatives, in 1996, Private Equity in Russia, in 1998, the Vanguard Group, in 1999, a series on long-term capital management, in 2007, before the financial
turns.zh: 他几乎以自己的哈佛商学院工作，逐字记录了现代金融的发展进程。举几个例子，在他众多案例中我最喜欢的包括：1994 年的 Black-Scholes 定价与 HP-12C 计算器，1990 年的 RJR Nabisco 杠杆收购，1994 年的 Bankers Trust 衍生品，1996 年的俄罗斯私募股权，1998 年的 Vanguard 集团，1999 年关于长期资本管理公司的一系列案例，以及 2007 年金融危机之前关于杠杆贷款的案例，

turns.en: crisis, a case on leveraged loans, and over the last decade, cases on the Notre Dame and Harvard Endowments. Among his directorships and trustee roles over the years, Andre is currently a board member at the Vanguard Group.
turns.zh: 还有过去十年关于圣母大学和哈佛捐赠基金的案例。在他多年担任的各种董事和受托人职务中，André 目前是 Vanguard 集团的董事会成员。

turns.en: In this episode, we spent the first 11 and a half minutes talking about teaching at Harvard, and then turned to the practice of investing, the active versus passive debate, a risk-based approach to asset allocation, and what makes investing so hard.
turns.zh: 在这一集中，我们用前 11 分半钟聊哈佛的教学，然后转向投资实践、主动与被动的争论、基于风险的资产配置方法，以及投资为什么如此之难。

turns.en: I found it fascinating hearing how Andre takes all of his academic experience and knowledge and applies it to the practice of investing at High Vista.
turns.zh: 我特别喜欢听 André 如何把他全部的学术经验与知识，应用到 HighVista 的投资实践中。

turns.en: His wisdom and clarity of thought are second to none, and his soothing South African accent only adds to the allure. If you like the show, please subscribe on iTunes, and maybe even write a review.
turns.zh: 他的智慧和思维的清晰度无人能及，而他那舒缓的南非口音更平添几分魅力。如果你喜欢这个节目，请在 iTunes 上订阅，也许还可以写条评论。

turns.en: You'll help others discover the podcast, and I thank you for it. And with that, I bring you my conversation with Andre Perreld. How did you first get interested in investing?
turns.zh: 这会帮助其他人发现这个播客，我对此感谢不尽。接下来，请听我和 André Perold 的对话。——你当初是怎么对投资产生兴趣的？

turns.en: So I sort of got into investing in a variety of ways. There were two essential aspects to it. One was I was always interested in probability and statistics.
turns.zh: 我进入投资领域有各种各样的路径，本质上两个方面。一方面，我一直对概率和统计很感兴趣。

turns.en: I was always trying to figure out odds, and investing is very much a game of odds. We were always trying to handicap outcomes, and so that was one side of it.
turns.zh: 我总是琢磨赔率，而投资很大程度上是赔率的游戏。我们总在给各种结果做让球估计，这是其中一面。

turns.en: Another side of it is I grew up in a family that had no money, and my parents figured out how to make everything, how to knit and sew and carpentry, and there was nothing.
turns.zh: 另一面是，我成长在一个没有钱的家庭，我父母什么都能自己搞定：编织、缝纫、木工，什么都没有——

turns.en: We made our own toys. And so from an early age, I did that myself, and I was always interested in how things worked. And that extended over time to how the world works.
turns.zh: 我们的玩具都是自制的。从很小的时候起，我就自己动手，一直对事物如何运作很感兴趣。而这种兴趣随着时间延伸到了世界如何运作。

turns.en: And investing is the best way or a fantastic way to think about how the world works. And so the combination of probability and statistics on the one hand and a sort of deep interest in how the world works combines to make investing a lot of fun.
turns.zh: 而投资是思考世界如何运作的极好方式。所以，概率统计这一端，加上对世界如何运作的深层兴趣，两相交汇，让投资变得非常好玩。

turns.en: What was the most rewarding thing for you about teaching? So I would say in academia, teaching is one of the great privileges in life. I think being able to have a place of honor where you're in front of a large group of very talented, or it doesn't matter if they're talented or not, students, and being able to engage them.
turns.zh: ——教学最有收获的是什么？——我想说，在学术界，教学是人生几大特权之一。能有一个令人羡慕的位置，站在一大群非常有才华的——有没有才华其实无所谓——学生面前，并且能和他们互动。

turns.en: There's a side conversation there. And I think it's a privilege to be able to teach, and I find for me teaching in the classroom is one part of teaching, but we're always teaching.
turns.zh: 这个话题还能岔出去聊很多。我觉得能教书是一种特权；对我来说，课堂上的教学只是教学的一部分，我们其实一直在教学。

turns.en: We're always helping other people. We're always, if you're selling your teaching, teaching shows up in everything you do. But I found teaching, besides helping others, it was very much a way to understand things.
turns.zh: 我们一直在帮助别人。如果你从事销售，教学的影子也出现在你做的每件事里。而且我发现，教学除了帮助别人，更是理解事物的一种方式。

turns.en: So I always loved to teach things, to teach about things I didn't really understand. Because if you can't explain something, you don't really understand it.
turns.zh: 所以我一直喜欢教一些我其实没完全弄懂的东西。因为如果你解释不清楚一件事，你就没有真正理解它。

turns.en: And so for me, teaching was a way to learn. I taught myself finance. I've taught myself a million things by just going into the classroom and trying to figure it out in the class with students.
turns.zh: 所以对我来说，教学就是学习。我自学了金融，靠走进课堂和学生一起把问题想明白，我自学了无数东西。

turns.en: And that's one of the greatest fun things to do. You started teaching at Harvard Business School at the age of 27, right? Yes. What was the average age of the students at the time?
turns.zh: 你 27 岁就开始在哈佛商学院教书了，对吧？是的。那当时学生的平均年龄多大？

turns.en: About the same. So go back to what was that like the first year? It was the blind leading the blind. Let's start there. When you walk into a Harvard Business School classroom, it's as intimidating as hell.
turns.zh: 也差不多。——那回想第一年，那是什么感觉？简直是盲人领盲人，先从那儿说起吧。走进哈佛商学院的教室，那种压迫感强得要命。

turns.en: And yet there's a sense that we're all in this to learn. It was nerve-racking. I got students who would come and see me. One in particular came to see me midway through the course to tell me what an absolutely terrible teacher I was.
turns.zh: 但同时又有一种我们大家都是来学习的氛围。那真的很紧张。有学生会来找我，其中一位专门在课程中途来告诉我，我教书教得有多烂。

turns.en: And the nice thing is by the end of the semester, we learned to like each other and they actually really liked it. I think it's just because they sort of appreciated that I was trying.
turns.zh: 好在到学期末，我们学会了彼此欣赏，他其实很喜欢那门课。我想是因为他看到了我确实在努力。

turns.en: And over time, you learn how to do it. You learn how to do it and you sort of grow into it. What does it take to be a good master of the classroom?
turns.zh: 慢慢地，你学会怎么做，你慢慢长成了那个角色。——要做一个掌控课堂的大师需要什么？

turns.en: Look, I think it takes humility, self-awareness. I think it's very interpersonal. You need to understand what they are thinking and struggling with.
turns.zh: 我觉得，需要谦逊和自我觉察。这东西非常讲究人际互动：你得理解他们在想什么、在挣扎什么。

turns.en: You need to think of ways to get people to see things. And so I would always spend a lot of time thinking about what questions I wanted to ask.
turns.zh: 你得想出办法让别人看见事物。所以我总会花大量时间琢磨我想提的问题。

turns.en: Questions that if I asked them, they could struggle with that question, that single question for a long time and it would shed a lot of light on something.
turns.zh: 那种一旦提出，就能让他们为一个问题苦思很久、并且照亮许多东西的问题。

turns.en: You know, sometimes a very simple question like what is a PE ratio and what do you do with it? Sounds easy and you can look it up in textbooks, but in fact when you peel away the layers of the onion, it's very deep and you can get into any and every aspect of investing through that simple little question.
turns.zh: 有时候一个非常朴素的问题，比如什么是市盈率、你拿它怎么办？听起来简单，教科书上一查就有，但层层剥开之后，它深得很：通过这个小小的问题，你可以切入投资的任何一面。

turns.en: So I think that's one. Another one is you really have to be willing to challenge your audience and make them think. I vividly remember you doing that.
turns.zh: 所以这是一点。另一点，你必须真的愿意挑战你的听众，逼他们思考。——我可记得你这样干过。

turns.en: You have to make them think and they respect that. They really respect that and when they come to class knowing they're going to be challenged, they prepare that much more.
turns.zh: 你得让他们思考，而他们尊重这一点。他们真心尊重。当他们来上课时知道自己会被挑战，准备就充分得多。

turns.en: They are deathly afraid of being embarrassed in front of their peers. And so when you do that, it's sort of a when, when, when and it just works.
turns.zh: 他们最怕在同侪面前出丑。所以你这么做，课堂就进入了那种提问、紧张、接住的节奏，一切都顺了。

turns.en: Were you teaching investing from the beginning, investment management straight through or did you evolve into that? No, I evolved into it. So my training was in a field called operations research.
turns.zh: 你一开始教的就是投资、一直是投资管理吗，还是后来演变过来的？——不，我是演变过来的。我受的训练在一个叫运筹学（operations research）的领域。

turns.en: It wasn't finance, which is sort of the math of doing stuff in business, scheduling and various things like that. And so I taught a course called managerial economics, which was about decision trees and statistics and game theory.
turns.zh: 不是金融。运筹学算是商业里做事的数学：排程和诸如此类的东西。所以我教的课叫管理经济学，讲决策树、统计和博弈论。

turns.en: But I was fascinated by investing and asked if they'd let me teach something I didn't know anything about and they did. And I taught myself.
turns.zh: 但我对投资着迷，就申请让我教一门自己一无所知的课，他们同意了。我就自学。

turns.en: And how many years in was that to your tenure? About three years, two years in. You certainly have taught lots of investment managers, hedge fund managers, probably lots of people in private equity as well.
turns.zh: 那是你任期里第几年？——大概第三年，两年左右。你肯定教过很多投资管理人和对冲基金经理，估计也有很多私募股权圈的人。

turns.en: Let's start with what were the characteristics that you found of good students in your classroom? And then the big question is going to be, was there a correlation with success and understanding investing investment management in the classroom and what people did later in their lives?
turns.zh: 我们先说说，你在课堂上发现好学生有什么特质？然后大问题来了：课堂上理解投资、投资管理的表现，和他们后来人生中的成就，有没有相关性？

turns.en: Look, the good students are good students in any setting. They're curious, they work hard, they go beyond what they're asked to do. At Harvard Business School, we demand that people are active learners.
turns.zh: 好学生到什么场景都是好学生。他们好奇、用功、做得比要求更多。哈佛商学院要求所有人做主动学习者。

turns.en: And so it's not enough to parrot something you've got to think hard about what's going on. In so many cases, the good students would draw upon their own experiences and bring it into the classroom and be very reflective about what they were learning and seeing and hearing.
turns.zh: 只会复述是不够的，你必须深度思考正在发生什么。很多情况下，好学生把自己的经历带进课堂，对自己学到、看到、听到的东西非常反思。

turns.en: And the good students were ones that moved the ball in the conversation, that they weren't just trying to make a point. They would understand what we were all struggling with and would help us along.
turns.zh: 好学生是那些把对话往前推进的人，而不是只想证明自己说得对。他们理解大家都在哪里卡住，帮助我们往前走。

turns.en: Even good didn't mean you knew what was going on, but just being unafraid to ask even a dumb question, they would actually help us all learn.
turns.zh: 甚至，优秀并不意味着什么都懂，而是不怕问一个笨问题——这样的人反而帮了我们所有人学习。

turns.en: Those were the good students and a lot of them did fabulously in the real world thereafter. These are personality traits that are pretty powerful in many settings.
turns.zh: 那就是好学生。他们中的很多人后来在现实世界里表现极好。——这些都是很有力量的人格特质，放到很多场景都成立。

turns.en: Harvard Business School, like anything else, is a business. And I'm curious if there are any parallels of some of the challenges that a school faces that a student who goes through wouldn't really understand.
turns.zh: 哈佛商学院和别的地方一样，也是一门生意。我好奇的是，学校面临的一些挑战，是不是学生走一遍也不会真正理解。

turns.en: But what actually happens in a school that makes it successful? Look, the first, the single most important thing about Harvard Business School is that Harvard Business School knows who it is.
turns.zh: 比如学校里到底实际发生了什么，才让它成功？——首先，哈佛商学院最重要的一点是：哈佛商学院知道自己是谁。

turns.en: It's grounded in practice. It cares about active learning in the classroom. It's not about lecturing. It's not about being extremely esoteric.
turns.zh: 它扎根于实践。它看重课堂上的主动学习，不靠讲授，也不刻意高深。

turns.en: And Harvard Business School is excellent at that. To pull it off, you need to attract and train faculty who can do it. It's very hard to do.
turns.zh: 哈佛商学院非常擅长这一点。要把它做成，你得吸引并培养能做这件事的师资，这非常难。

turns.en: Because when you're the only school doing it, when you're doing something very unique, it requires a heroic effort all the time to make sure that you can actually pull it off.
turns.zh: 因为当只有你一家这么做、当你做着一件非常独特的事时，你需要时时付出英雄般的努力，确保真的能把它做成。

turns.en: And it's a little bit like a religion where you're always fighting to keep the flock coming to church and the same thing here. And I think Harvard Business School is extremely good at doing that.
turns.zh: 这有点像宗教：你要不断争取教众来教堂，这里也是一样。我觉得哈佛商学院极为擅长这件事。

turns.en: So one of the things that, I guess, Harvard Business School professors often have advisory consulting projects to be active in the real world, as you said.
turns.zh: 我想，哈佛商学院的教授们常常有顾问或咨询项目，像你说的，参与真实世界。

turns.en: And one of yours has been a long time association with Vanguard. Today, and we'll certainly spend a lot more time talking about this, you are an active manager.
turns.zh: 而你与 Vanguard 的长期合作就是其中之一。今天——我们肯定还会多聊——你是一位主动管理者。

turns.en: And Vanguard has a lot of active products, but it's particularly well known for passive management. It seems that active versus passive is on a lot of people's minds these days.
turns.zh: Vanguard 有很多主动产品，但它尤其以被动管理著称。似乎最近很多人心里都在琢磨主动与被动这个话题。

turns.en: And I was wondering if you could weigh in, given that you're so much deeper in the actual practice of what Vanguard does and understand it so much more than most.
turns.zh: 我想知道，鉴于你对 Vanguard 实际所做之事的理解比绝大多数人深得多，你能否来谈谈——

turns.en: And yet you also are an active manager, investing in active managers. How do you feel about all of this? So look, I think the first thing to say is Vanguard, as you just said, has a lot of active product.
turns.zh: ——而你同时又是主动管理者、还把钱投给主动管理者，你怎么看这一切？——首先我想说，Vanguard 像你刚才讲的，有大量主动产品。

turns.en: A very significant part of our AUM is in actively managed funds, equities, various kinds of fixed income, things like that. Vanguard is known for indexing, but the key is to understand it's also doing so at very low cost.
turns.zh: 我们 AUM 中相当大的一部分在主动管理基金里：股票、各种固定收益，诸如此类。Vanguard 以指数化闻名，但关键在于理解它同时也做到了极低成本。

turns.en: And so they ring costs out of the system in a very efficient way. And the combination of products that perform as advertised, so when you're tracking an index, you track the index at a low cost, is a very powerful idea that gives them a huge advantage.
turns.zh: 他们非常高效地把成本从系统里剔除。再加上产品如宣传所述运作——跟踪指数就真能低成本地跟踪指数——这个组合是非常有力的理念，给了他们巨大优势。

turns.en: Indexing, the way I think about indexing is it's very simple. You either do or don't have an edge in investing. And each of us, most people have no edge ever in investing and some people have an edge some of the time.
turns.zh: 我是这样理解指数化的：它很简单。你在投资上要么有优势（edge），要么没有。大多数人永远都没有优势，有些人在有些时候有优势。

turns.en: And the key is to know when do you have an edge and when do you not. You may have an edge at a particular point in time because you know something about something you're very familiar or expert in a certain area that happens to be ripe for investing.
turns.zh: 关键是知道什么时候你有优势、什么时候没有。你可能在某个时点有优势，因为你对你非常熟悉的东西有了解，或在某个恰好适合投资的领域是专家。

turns.en: You may have an industry expertise or something or knowledge about something where you can take advantage of it. I think some people think they have an edge all the time.
turns.zh: 你可能有行业专长或某种知识，可以利用它。我觉得有些人以为自己永远有优势。

turns.en: That's a big mistake. And most people have no edge at any point in time. And so the way I think about it is when you do have an edge, by all means try and take advantage of it.
turns.zh: 那是大错特错。而大多数人任何时候都没有优势。所以我的想法是：当你确实有优势时，务必设法利用它。

turns.en: The edge might be also knowing certain managers who are very good. You know, just give money to others who actually may have an edge and pay them a fee for it.
turns.zh: 优势也可能体现在认识某些真正优秀的管理人。你可以把钱交给那些真正可能有优势的人，并为此付给他们费用。

turns.en: But most people don't. And if you don't have an edge, you should probably index. It still doesn't answer the question of how you invest because you have to decide how to allocate your assets across different asset categories.
turns.zh: 但大多数人没有优势。没有优势，就最好去做指数化。不过这仍没有回答怎么投的问题，因为你还得决定把资产分配到不同的大类。

turns.en: But as a way of executing, well, indexing is very good for folks who don't have an edge. At High Vista, we do that all the time when we don't have an edge somewhere and don't see opportunities will totally buy indices as a placeholder until we do.
turns.zh: 但作为一种执行方式，指数化对没有优势的人非常好。在 HighVista，当我们某处没有优势、看不到机会时，我们随时直接买指数作为占位，直到我们看到机会。

turns.en: Warren Buffett, I think, said it very nicely. He said when dumb money acknowledges its limitations, it sees us to be dumb. And so folks who index, at least they'll track the index and not be taken advantage of.
turns.zh: 我想 Warren Buffett 说得特别漂亮。他说，当笨钱承认了自己的局限，它就不再是笨钱。所以做指数的人，至少能跟上指数，而不会被人占便宜。

turns.en: And that's a very powerful thing to understand. So now, I guess 13-ish years ago, you started High Vista strategies. What was the light bulb that went off in your head that said, hey, I got to go do this?
turns.zh: ——这是非常有力的认知。那么大概 13 年前，你创立了 HighVista Strategies。当时脑子里那个灯泡是什么时候亮的——我必须出去干这件事？

turns.en: So I had spent my academic life thinking about many aspects of investing, about asset allocation, about trying to outperform, thinking about where you could get an edge, understanding the business of hedge funds and other investment firms.
turns.zh: 我把整个学术生涯都用来思考投资的很多方面：资产配置、如何跑赢、优势可能从哪里来，以及理解对冲基金和其他投资机构这门生意。

turns.en: And you think questions like currency hedging, questions like how do you minimize execution costs, questions about how do you reshape the probability distribution, all sorts of questions relating to just about every facet of investing, how do you do securities lending, and why would you do it and when.
turns.zh: 你研究的问题包括货币对冲、如何最小化执行成本、如何重塑概率分布——几乎所有投资层面的问题，比如证券借贷怎么做、为什么做、什么时候做。

turns.en: And having studied all that, when the idea of High Vista came along, the idea being to invest in a single fund in everything and everything, anything and everything that moved the way the large endowments do, it's called unfettered investing.
turns.zh: 在研究了所有这些之后，HighVista 的想法出现了：在一只基金里投一切可投的东西——任何东西、只要有吸引力，就像大型捐赠基金那样。他们称之为 unfettered investing，无拘束的投资。

turns.en: It just really appealed to me because I could draw on everything I'd studied until then, including risk management and all those kinds of things.
turns.zh: 它对我极具吸引力，因为我可以调用我此前研究过的每一样东西，包括风险管理和种种相关内容。

turns.en: And what are your core beliefs about investing? Someone who has an approach, who's allocating capital, has to start with the philosophy. What is yours?
turns.zh: 那么你对投资的核心信条是什么？一个有方法论、在做资本配置的人，必须从哲学出发——你的哲学是什么？

turns.en: So look, I think at High Vista we think about two things. One is we think about how do we, where and how can we outperform by finding extraordinary managers to give money to?
turns.zh: 我想，在 HighVista 我们考虑两件事。一是：我们在哪里、如何通过找到优秀管理人并把钱交给他们来跑赢？

turns.en: Where and how can we outperform by doing things in-house that are fairly simple strategies where we may be able to earn an extra return without being too clever?
turns.zh: 二是：我们在哪里、如何通过内部自己做相对简单的策略来跑赢——也许能在不用太聪明的情况下多赚一点回报？

turns.en: Think of all of that as how do you execute on trying to earn alpha in the area and then combine that with sort of trying to think pretty deeply about risk and be very deliberate about the risks we are taking and try and manage to those risk targets that we set for ourselves.
turns.zh: 把这一切都看作如何执行、如何赚取 alpha，然后再加上对风险的深入思考，非常审慎地对待我们承担的风险，努力朝我们设定的风险目标去管理。

turns.en: And so has that started the one fund? Does that start with a certain type of asset allocation? It starts with a level of risk that we want to take and we try and quantify what that risk is.
turns.zh: 所以这是从那只单一基金开始的吗？它是从某种资产配置开始——它从我们想要承担的风险水平开始，我们试着把那个风险量化出来。

turns.en: Risk to us is four at the level of a portfolio, what is the probability of losing X dollars over a certain period of time, something like a year or you know and then try and quantify those risks based on how we're invested and the world is a very dynamic place and as risks evolve in the markets it was pretty risky time in the world in 08, it's a lot calmer time in the world today and you think very differently about risk when you're in different
turns.zh: 对我们来说，风险在组合层面就是：在一段时期内，比如一年，亏损 X 美元的概率是多少？然后基于我们的持仓把这些风险量化出来。世界非常动态，风险随市场演化——2008 年是个非常危险的时刻，今天的世界平静得多。在不同市场环境中，你对风险的看法会非常不同。

turns.en: kinds of market environments and trying to be very cognizant of those environments and reflect that in the portfolio as we think about risk is pretty important.
turns.zh: 所以在思考风险时，充分意识到这些环境并把它们反映到组合里，相当重要。

turns.en: So a lot of people if you think about how Warren Buffett might talk about risk the time horizon really impacts what that means to say you're going to lose money over a specified period of time.
turns.zh: 很多人——比如想想 Warren Buffett 谈风险的方式——时间长度确实会影响在一段时期内亏钱意味着什么。

turns.en: When you set that up for Hivista is that tied to the business and therefore the liquidity that you provide your investors as the metric of risk?
turns.zh: 在 HighVista，你会把这个和风险同业务绑在一起吗——也就是，把你为投资者提供的流动性，作为风险的度量？

turns.en: Absolutely, I think we all have to understand that our capital is from a given source at any point in time. Any firm has capital from some source and capital often moves for good reasons and sometimes for not so good reasons.
turns.zh: 绝对如此。我认为我们都必须理解：在任何时点，我们的资本都来自某个特定的来源。任何公司的资本都有来源，而资本的流动往往有正当理由，有时理由并不那么好。

turns.en: The good reasons are people need to spend, they want to buy a house, they want to buy something, make a capital investment and they need the money and those are good reasons.
turns.zh: 正当的理由包括：人们需要花钱、想买房子、想买点什么、要做资本开支，他们需要钱，这些是好理由。

turns.en: The less good reasons are when people are afraid, they suddenly get fearful, they suddenly get very euphoric and optimistic about markets and want to chase returns and they move around for psychological reasons that sometimes are not so good.
turns.zh: 不那么好的理由是：人们害怕了——突然恐惧，突然对市场极度亢奋乐观、追逐回报。他们因为心理因素调仓，而这些理由有时并不好。

turns.en: So one has to understand your client base, you always want to educate your client base as to what you do and keep the clients you know, confident that the kinds of things you're trying to do for them are really in their best interests.
turns.zh: 所以你必须理解你的客户基础，永远要教育你的客户，让他们了解你在做什么，并让他们确信，你在为他们做的事情确实符合他们的最佳利益。

turns.en: But it isn't always the case, Warren Buffett has the absolutely wonderful benefit that he has permanent capital and it completely changes what he can do because he has permanent capital than any other investor can do who does not have permanent capital.
turns.zh: 但并不总是能做到。Warren Buffett 有一个绝对美妙的条件：他拥有永久性资本（permanent capital），这彻底改变了他能做的事情——任何其他没有永久资本的投资者都做不到。

turns.en: Risk if you're measuring it in the markets, commonly volatility, lots of investors think that's not a great metric of risk and yet I'm not sure if you're trying to calculate risks across different asset classes, what else you would use.
turns.zh: 如果在市场里衡量风险，通常就是波动率。很多投资者觉得它不是很好的风险指标，可我又觉得，如果你想跨资产类别计算风险，好像也没有别的更好用的。

turns.en: How do you think about that? So we've done a lot of research on risk at the portfolio level versus at the individual security level. And I think the first thing to say is at the individual security level, volatility need not be a good measure of risk at all.
turns.zh: 你怎么看这个问题？——我们做了大量组合层面与单只证券层面的风险研究。我想先说的是：在单只证券层面，波动率根本未必是好风险度量。

turns.en: You know, a strategy that sells options and has limited upside and big downside, you're not going to detect that from volatility statistics.
turns.zh: 比如一个卖出期权的策略，上行有限、下行巨大——你不会从波动率统计里发现这一点。

turns.en: Examples might be credit investments that give you a small nice return for a long time and then suddenly blow up. I think at the portfolio level, if you're diversified, your biggest exposures are to the broad markets, usually the equity markets.
turns.zh: 例子可能是信用投资：很长时间给你一个不高不低、挺舒服的小回报，然后突然爆掉。我认为在组合层面，如果你做了分散化，你最大的敞口通常是对大盘、也就是股票市场的敞口。

turns.en: Exposure to the equity markets is your biggest risk. And there there's very strong evidence that when things are volatile, thereafter the risk of a big drawdown is much higher than when things are calm.
turns.zh: 对股票市场的敞口就是你最大的风险。而有很强证据表明：波动大的时候，之后出现大幅回撤的概率，远高于风平浪静的时候。

turns.en: Thereafter. Thereafter. So it's not so usually volatility is associated with times of stress. That's correct. What happens, what is so striking is that once you have volatility, it tends to continue.
turns.zh: 之后——我是说之后。——所以波动率通常和压力时期相伴，对吧？——没错。真正惊人的是：一旦波动率起来了，它往往会持续。

turns.en: And if there's if things are volatile today, the risk of a big drawdown are much higher tomorrow than if things are not so volatile today. A very simple idea.
turns.zh: 如果今天波动很大，那么明天出现大幅回撤的概率，就比今天平静时高得多。一个非常简单的想法。

turns.en: It's very effective. We use that idea as part of what we do. There are related ideas that go with that ideas like correlation. How are things moving together?
turns.zh: 它非常有效。我们工作中就用这个想法。还有一些相关的概念，比如相关性：事物之间是如何联动运动的？

turns.en: How are they moving together today? Volatility versus could be different from how they may have moved together in the past. The idea of correlation, the idea of volatility as a predictor of risk, these are all very useful concepts that work at the portfolio level.
turns.zh: 它们今天的联动方式，可能和过去的联动方式不同。相关性这个概念、波动率作为风险的预测器，这些在组合层面都是非常有用的概念。

turns.en: They may or may not be helpful. A lot of that those metrics are tied to public markets. Volatility doesn't matter if someone's investing in private equity and giving them their money for 10 years.
turns.zh: 它们也许有用，也许没有。那些指标大多绑定公开市场。有人投私募股权、把钱放十年，波动率对他就不重要。

turns.en: So how do you balance the public market where you can measure those risks and investments in private markets where you're kind of setting it and forgetting it for a while?
turns.zh: 那你怎么平衡：一边是公开市场——可以衡量风险；一边是私募市场——投了就先放一阵子？

turns.en: So I think one has to think of illiquid investments as risky in many ways. So something can be illiquid, yet the underlying assets can be in public instruments.
turns.zh: 我认为得把非流动性投资视为在很多意义上是有风险的。一个东西可能本身非流动，但底层资产可以是公开市场工具。

turns.en: For example, a hedge fund with long dated lockups is an example of an illiquid asset, your investment in the hedge fund, but the underlying is liquid.
turns.zh: 比如一个有长期锁定期（lockup）的对冲基金：你在对冲基金的投资是非流动的，但底层是流动的。

turns.en: So you can get a sense for the risk of your investment with that hedge fund. But the fact is there are other factors that affect the risk of the hedge fund.
turns.zh: 所以你可以大致把握对这个对冲基金投资的风险。但事实是，还有其他因素会影响对冲基金的风险。

turns.en: Their clients may suddenly want to redeem or the person may want to change their mind as to what they really want to do. There's a variety of risks that could occur.
turns.zh: 他们的客户可能突然要赎回，或者这个人自己可能改变主意、不想再做同样的事。可能发生各种各样的风险。

turns.en: There could be a ban on short selling like we saw in 2008. You got to think about all of those risks, even though the underlying assets are liquid.
turns.zh: 还可能像 2008 年那样禁止做空。所有这些风险你都得考虑，即便底层资产是流动的。

turns.en: Then of course there are assets that are illiquid, inherently illiquid, such as in private equity, private loans, private many things. And there you need to understand you're making a bet that something will work over a long period of time.
turns.zh: 然后当然也有天然就非流动的资产，比如私募股权、私募贷款，很多私募的东西。在那里，你得理解：你是在赌一件事能在很长时期里行得通。

turns.en: And a lot of things have to go right for those things to work over a long period of time. They may seem great today, but when you make a long dated commitment you're assuming that things will be in place for the duration.
turns.zh: 要让这些东西在长时期里管用，得有很多东西配合到位。它们今天看起来可能很好，但当你做一个长期承诺时，你默认了各种条件在整个期限内都成立。

turns.en: And at the very least there's an opportunity cost. You can't change your mind very easily. The world is very dynamic and changes and you may find that you're stuck and it's pretty costly that you tied your hands.
turns.zh: 至少还有机会成本：你没法轻易改主意。世界非常动态、不断变化，你可能发现自己被困住了，这种束手束脚代价不菲。

turns.en: On the other hand, often you tie your hands and you get handsomely rewarded for that and you always have to balance those two concerns. This is ultimately a people business and you've worked with, you've taught lots of people over the years.
turns.zh: 但另一方面，很多时候你束住手脚，反而会得到丰厚回报，你永远要在两个诉求之间平衡。——说到底这是一门关于人的生意。这些年你共事过、教过很多人。

turns.en: How do you get inside the heads of the people you're thinking of investing in to really get comfort that you're ready to commit capital to them?
turns.zh: 你怎么钻进你考虑投资的那些人的脑子里，真正安心地把资本承诺给他们？

turns.en: So that's a really hard question. I think talent, identifying talent is really hard. Sometimes you know there's talent. You know they're exactly what you want, but they're so good you can't get in.
turns.zh: 这是很难的问题。识别人才真的很难。有时候你知道有人才，你知道他们正是你要的，可他们太好，你根本挤不进去。

turns.en: So the issue is, so the hardest cases are usually the ones where someone will take your money, you always have to ask why you're so lucky, but they'll take your money, you think they're very talented, but you have to convince yourself.
turns.zh: 所以最难的情况往往是：有人愿意收你的钱——你永远得问自己凭什么这么幸运——你觉得他们非常有才华，但你还得说服自己。

turns.en: But it's not just talent, it's are they talented? What is the opportunity that they're pursuing? Is that opportunity still in place? Do they have a team that can execute?
turns.zh: 而且不只是才华，还有：他们真的有才华吗？他们追求的机会还在吗？他们有能执行的团队吗？

turns.en: Remember this talent is also running a business. Are they good business managers? They have to worry about their clients and keep them happy.
turns.zh: 别忘了，这些有才华的人还在经营一家公司。他们是好的经营管理者吗？他们得照顾客户、让客户满意。

turns.en: They need to attract a talent to work for them and mentor and keep those folks happy. And you're asking an awful lot of somebody, so you need multifaceted talent at the very least where you're making a commitment to them.
turns.zh: 他们还得吸引人才来工作、培养并留住这些人。你对一个人要求的实在太多，所以至少需要多层面的才华，尤其是你要把钱托付给他们的时候。

turns.en: I would say it's pretty hard. It's pretty hard. After the fact it's of course always easy, but there are a lot of folks who are on paper extraordinarily talented who end up not performing so well after the fact as we all know.
turns.zh: 我想说这很难，真的很难。事后看当然总是容易，但很多纸面上才华横溢的人，事后表现并不那么好，这我们谁都见过。

turns.en: So you need to make judgments. I think the ability to judge people is an essential skill that one needs and it's very hard. Everything seems like it's hard today.
turns.zh: 所以你必须学会做判断。我认为识人能力是一项必备的手艺，而且非常难。——现在看什么都是难的。

turns.en: Markets, you talk to people, everybody says markets are expensive, asset classes are expensive. You are tasked with making money for your clients.
turns.zh: 市场也好，跟人聊天也罢，所有人都说市场贵、资产类别贵。而你的任务是替客户赚钱。

turns.en: Where are you seeing opportunities? So let's understand why it's hard. It's hard because the world's competitive. It's also hard because the world doesn't stand still.
turns.zh: 你在哪里看到机会？——我们先弄清楚为什么难。难是因为世界是竞争的；难还因为世界不会静止不动。

turns.en: And so the industry is always evolving. If you have a good idea, the odds are high. Others have that same idea. So I think investing is always hard.
turns.zh: 这个行业一直在演化。如果你有一个好主意，大概率别人也有同样的主意。所以我觉得投资永远都难。

turns.en: It's harder than you think. It's the same as any other aspect of business. If you try and compete as a firm, it doesn't matter who you are, this competition, it's seldom easy.
turns.zh: 它比你想的更难。这和做生意的其他任何领域一样：你去竞争，不论你是谁，竞争很少是轻松的。

turns.en: And so I would just say this idea that there are times when it's easy and there are times that it's hard. I think it's hard all the time. I think in today's world, I think it is hard.
turns.zh: 所以我就想说：有时容易、有时难这个说法——我觉得是一直难。在今天的世界上，我觉得确实难。

turns.en: It's hard to see anything obvious. Equity markets are high. It's hard to sort of have a belief that equity market returns will be fantastic over the next 10 years.
turns.zh: 很难看到什么显而易见的机会。股票市场位置很高，你很难抱有一种信念，认为未来 10 年股票的回报会很出色。

turns.en: I think we sort of think about it in sort of along two dimensions. One is there's a very dynamic aspect to the world and it may be that there may not be great places to put money today, but there will be in the future and you need to prepare yourself for those instances.
turns.zh: 我想我们大致从两个维度来思考。一是世界有非常动态的一面：今天也许没有好去处，但未来会有，你得为那些时刻做好准备。

turns.en: So we think of managers who have flexible mandates, for example, as being a prime candidate for folks we want to partner with, folks that are prepared for things.
turns.zh: 所以我们认为，灵活委托（flexible mandate）的管理人，是我们特别想合作的那种人——他们是有准备的人。

turns.en: Being prepared takes work. Being prepared and not investing is very hard because it looks like you're not doing anything. But the fact is you need to be good enough to guess where the opportunities might be and then the minute they occur you have to jump and pounce on them.
turns.zh: 准备是要下功力的。准备了却不投资也非常难受，因为你看起来像什么都没做。但事实是，你得足够好去预判机会可能在哪里，一旦它出现，立刻跳起来扑上去。

turns.en: So finding firms that are good at that is one of the things that we're always looking for. On the basis that the world's very dynamic and it's the day you buy is when you make your money, not the day you sell.
turns.zh: 找到擅长这个的公司，是我们一直在看的事之一。理由是：世界高度动态，而且你赚钱是在买入那天，不是卖出那天。

turns.en: And being ready for those buying opportunities is sort of critical. That's one kind. The other kind is looking for niches where specialists can outperform and just thinking about very nichey off the run areas.
turns.zh: 为那些买入机会做好准备是关键。这是一种。另一种是寻找专家能跑赢的缝隙市场，想想那些非常冷门、不在主流赛道上的领域。

turns.en: Example might be direct lending, for example. The lending space is interesting because banks have exited vast swaths of the lending space and I think there's money to be made there.
turns.zh: 例子比如直接借贷。借贷市场很有意思，因为银行退出了大片借贷空间，我觉得那里能赚钱。

turns.en: And there are other areas, nichey areas that are a little off the run where you find a team that can do well and then you just have to keep reaffirming A that it's the right team and B that the opportunity set is still there.
turns.zh: 还有其他一些冷门、非主流的领域：找到一个能做得好的团队，然后你必须不断重新确认两件事——A，这是对的人；B，机会池还在。

turns.en: We're going to take a quick break in the action to tell you about Brookfield. Brookfield invests in the thing behind the thing behind the next big thing.
turns.zh: 我们中途插播一条 Brookfield 的广告。Brookfield 投资于下一个大事件背后的背后的东西。

turns.en: Their focus across infrastructure, energy, real estate, private equity and credit is helping to build the backbone of the global economy. Brookfield combines deep operational expertise with disciplined long-term investing, uncovering value and partnering alongside clients to shape tomorrow's economy today.
turns.zh: 他们在基础设施、能源、房地产、私募股权和信贷领域的布局，正在帮助搭建全球经济的脊梁。Brookfield 把深厚的运营专长与纪律严明的长期投资相结合，发掘价值，与客户并肩，在今天塑造明天的经济。

turns.en: Invest in the businesses that shape tomorrow. Learn how you can own what's next at Brookfield.com slash own. This is not an offer to sell or investment advice.
turns.zh: 投资于塑造明天的企业。到 Brookfield.com/own 了解如何拥有未来。这不是出售要约，也不构成投资建议。

turns.en: Investing involves risk, including the loss of capital. And now, back to the show. Are there any particular niches that you're excited about today?
turns.zh: 投资有风险，包括损失本金的可能。——好，回到节目。——今天有什么细分领域让你特别兴奋吗？

turns.en: I think if you look at areas like biotech, there are a lot of smaller biotech companies that are not well understood at all. People love, it's sort of fattish and people chase things based on psychology.
turns.zh: 我觉得像生物科技：有很多小型生物科技公司完全不被市场理解。人们各有偏好，会根据心理追热点。

turns.en: It's a particularly nice area to be able to try and play that game. I think smaller banks are an area as well where you see they just not very glamorous kinds of things and you just need to go from one to the next and try to understand what they're doing.
turns.zh: 所以那里很适合玩这个游戏，是个不错的领域。我觉得小型银行也是一个领域——就是那种不那么光鲜的事，你得一家一家去看，理解他们在做什么。

turns.en: But there's just a very broad range of these things. Small cap activism is another one where these are, again, off the run things. They're not buying the large caps and doing things like that, although the large caps themselves are not all of them are that expensive and there are opportunities, it seems, there as well.
turns.zh: 但这类机会其实非常广泛。小盘股东行动主义（small cap activism）也是又一类冷门领域。他们不去买大盘股做事。当然大盘股本身并非全都贵——我觉得那里也有机会。

turns.en: So you and your team spend all this time exploring these niches, trying to find these great opportunities you're hunting where other people aren't.
turns.zh: 你和你的团队花大量时间探索这些细分领域，去猎寻别人没在找的好机会。

turns.en: And at the same time, the studies all say that asset allocation drives returns. So if you step back from the biotech investing, the small cap banks, small cap activism, the banks, what does your overall asset allocation look like today?
turns.zh: 但同时，研究都说资产配置驱动回报。所以先跳出生物科技、小盘银行、小盘行动主义，你整体的资产配置现在是什么样的？

turns.en: And does it jive with sort of how much time do you spend at that level as opposed to really looking at the underneath the corners to execute as well as you can?
turns.zh: 你在这个层面花多少时间，和你真正深入角落、把执行尽可能做好的时间相比，如何搭配？

turns.en: Look, so I think of it very differently. I would say, you know, people, I think there's a bit of a false dichotomy that people draw between what's more important, manager selection or asset allocation.
turns.zh: 我的看法非常不同。我觉得所谓管理人选择和资产配置哪个更重要，多少是个伪命题。

turns.en: So let me first say, if you're selecting managers who can't outperform, then it's a problem you should just index and be done. And then it's all about asset allocation.
turns.zh: 先说：如果你选的管理人没有能力跑赢，那是个问题——你干脆做指数就好了。那时一切才都是资产配置。

turns.en: If you can find managers who can add a lot of alpha, it changes the game completely. And then it's a function of how many of those do you have?
turns.zh: 但如果你能找到增加大量 alpha 的管理人，游戏规则就完全变了，接下来取决于你有多少这样的管理人。

turns.en: If you have all your money split between three managers who are very active in what they do but really good, I think it's all about managers.
turns.zh: 如果你所有的钱都分给三个管理人，他们操作非常主动、又非常优秀——那我觉得一切关于管理人。

turns.en: And I think, so it's, you know, if you're highly diversified across managers, that's a different story, then most of what they do cancels out and you're left with beta risk, which is about asset allocation.
turns.zh: 而如果管理人高度分散，故事就不同了：他们做的事大部分相互抵消，剩下的就是 beta 风险，那才是资产配置。

turns.en: We sort of think about it as, look, we finding alpha is, alpha is scarce, finding alpha is hard and you need to find it where it is. You find alpha most of the time where there are dislocations, where there are capital shortages in the world.
turns.zh: 我们的思路是：alpha 稀缺，寻找 alpha 很难，你得在它所在的地方找到它。alpha 大多出现在错位的地方、出现在世界上资本短缺的地方。

turns.en: You don't find alpha all the time, but on the corner of Fifth Avenue and 47th. It just doesn't sit there all the time. You may occasionally, but it doesn't sit there all the time.
turns.zh: 你不会在第五大道和 47 街的路口随时捡到 alpha。偶尔可能，但它不会总在那里。

turns.en: So you need to go where it is. And it may be it's there in Japan. It may be there. It's there in distressed investing. It may be it's in some place and you need to go there.
turns.zh: 所以你得去它在的地方。也许在日本，也许在困境投资，也许在某个地方，你得走过去。

turns.en: So our view is alpha, the pursuit of alpha is always opportunistic. And you must go where it is, not where you'd like it to be conveniently.
turns.zh: 所以我们的观点是：追求 alpha 永远是机会主义的。必须去它在的地方，而不是你希望它刚好在你方便之处的地方。

turns.en: When you find it, invest in it, unless there's some reason it doesn't make sense. And that always leaves you with an idiosyncratic set of managers and an idiosyncratic exposures to the broad markets because each place you find, each pond you find has its own set of exposures to the broad market.
turns.zh: 找到它就投进去，除非有理由不该投。这样留下的必然是一组非典型的管理人、以及对大盘非典型的敞口——因为你发现的每一个水塘，都有自己的大盘敞口。

turns.en: So you can get pretty lopsided exposures if you follow money opportunistically, if you follow the opportunities where they are. And so our view is look for the opportunities where they are and then true up the exposures you get so that your overall exposures make sense.
turns.zh: 如果随机会而动，你可能会得到相当失衡的敞口。所以我们的观点是：先去找机会所在，再把由此产生的敞口配平，让整体敞口说得过去。

turns.en: So how much U.S. equity exposure am I getting by virtue of these terrific opportunities? And if it's less than I would like, add to it, perhaps in a passive way.
turns.zh: 比如：因为这些绝佳机会，我已经拿到多少美国股票敞口？如果比我想要的少，就加上一点——也许用被动的方式加。

turns.en: And if it's more than I really want, I can hedge it out. And that bounds, is that sort of there's ranges that you're comfortable with? That's where the risk target really matters.
turns.zh: 如果超过我真正想要的，我可以把它对冲掉。——所以有边界，有你觉得舒服的区间？——风险目标在这里才真正重要。

turns.en: So we are very risk conscious and a portion of our capitals in a very low risk fund and there the ranges are much lower for equity exposure than they would be in a higher risk version.
turns.zh: 我们风险意识很强，一部分资本放在极低风险的基金里，那里股票敞口的区间比高风险版本低得多。

turns.en: So we set those based on a broad sense of risk and just depends on the risk target. I found in my time at Protégé that when you're looking for the great opportunities, you like your team who's out talking to people to also be looking at.
turns.zh: 所以我们会基于对风险的总体感觉来设定这些，取决于风险目标。——我在 Protégé 的时候发现，寻找绝佳机会时，你喜欢让在外面跟人交流的团队也到处在看。

turns.en: But I also found there was a lot more art than science into being able to spot what is a great opportunity. And that takes a lot of experience and there's only, you only have a limited bandwidth.
turns.zh: 但我也发现，识别什么是绝佳机会这件事，艺术远多于科学，需要大量经验，而你的带宽是有限的。

turns.en: How do you try to get the people on your team to be looking opportunistically across around the world? Look, I think it's hard and it's easy.
turns.zh: 你们怎么让团队在全球范围机会性地搜寻？——我觉得这事既难又不难。

turns.en: The easy part is it's amazing the inbound traffic that we get. When you have money, people want to talk to you. It's shocking that when we have money, people want to talk to us.
turns.zh: 不难的部分是：我们收到的主动上门机会多得惊人。当你手里有钱，大家都想来跟你聊。

turns.en: And so that's one of the things. So the issue is you are chasing down a whole range of things. Often there are opportunities you can't find the team.
turns.zh: 这是一方面。真正的问题是，你在追一大堆东西。常常是有机会但找不到合适的团队。

turns.en: Often there are opportunities and you can find the team, but the terms don't work. It's too long a lock up or it's too expensive along some dimensions.
turns.zh: 常常是有机会也能找到团队，但条款不合适：锁定期太长，或在某些维度上太贵。

turns.en: Sometimes it's too expensive because of taxes. And so even though you might see something, you don't have a way to execute on it. And we work hard to try and find ways to execute.
turns.zh: 有时是税务原因太贵。于是即使你看到了机会，也没有办法去执行。我们很努力地在寻找可行的执行方式。

turns.en: Sometimes there are ways to execute through derivatives or some other way of doing something or create a sort of an LP friendly structure that sort of helps.
turns.zh: 有时可以通过衍生品或别的方法执行，或者搭一个对 LP 友好的结构来帮忙。

turns.en: But I think in each case one just has to, this is where being an investor really helps. And having an investment mindset where you have to put yourself in the shoes of the folks making these investments and ask yourself, if you were doing these, would you see it the same way and it's very much the same kind of work that someone would do is actually doing it and making those investment decisions.
turns.zh: 但我觉得在每个案例里，投资人身份本身真的帮忙。带着投资思维，把自己放到做这些投资的人的位置上问自己：如果你在做同样的事，你会不会一样看它？这和实际做决策的人要做的功课是一模一样的。

turns.en: So we all learn from our mistakes. Can you talk about what you've learned in this period of time over the last decade that's different from what you thought investment firms did or had to do to execute well when you were teaching and studying firms?
turns.zh: 我们都从错误中学习。过去这十年，你学到了什么——与你当老师和研究者时以为投资公司做好所必需的样子不同的东西？

turns.en: I think the biggest lesson has been that the world is extremely competitive and that competitiveness is not something you see until later in a given area.
turns.zh: 我觉得最大的教训是：世界极其竞争，而这种竞争性往往要到一个领域发展的后期才看得见。

turns.en: So you think you found something, you think you're the first to see it or maybe the second or the third and you realize later that you were just one of many and it's already competed away before you can actually take advantage of it.
turns.zh: 你以为你找到了什么，以为自己是第一个看到的，或第二第三，然后后来发现你只是其中之一——在你来得及利用之前，它早就被竞争掉了。

turns.en: It's so surprising to see after the fact how things almost always don't work out nearly as well as you thought they did before the fact, you're always disappointed.
turns.zh: 事后看，你会发现事情几乎从来不如事前想的那么好，你永远会失望，这很惊人。

turns.en: It's a bit like golf. Yeah. You're always disappointed. You hope springs eternal. You know, outside of the story it goes both ways because I remember being involved in the subprime short and it was a perfect trade and you looked at it and you mapped it out and you said, boy, if this goes as we think, we're going to pay 8% and we're going to make 10 times our money and then it worked.
turns.zh: 有点像高尔夫。是的，你永远会失望。希望永远都在。不过说回来，这事有两面——因为我记得当年我们参与了次贷做空，那是一笔完美的交易：你研究它、画出路线图，然后说，如果真像我们想的这样，付 8% 的成本，能赚 10 倍——然后它成了。

turns.en: And one of the things you saw afterwards with some of the people who were in that trade without pointing to any particular manager is that it almost changed the way they thought.
turns.zh: 而事后让我观察到——不点名任何特定管理人——参与那笔交易的某些人，那几乎改变了他们的思维方式。

turns.en: They did something that was perfect and then they proceeded to search for the next thing that was perfect and if it wasn't the big grand slam home run, they couldn't do it the same way anymore.
turns.zh: 他们做成了一笔完美的交易，然后就开始寻找下一笔完美的。如果它不是那种大满贯本垒打，他们就再也做不出同样的味道了。

turns.en: Look, I couldn't agree more and what that says is that there's a huge amount of luck in our business. So subprime worked in two ways. One it was just a good trade where if housing did badly, you could do well.
turns.zh: 我完全同意。这说明我们这行里有大量的运气成分。次贷那笔交易有两层含义。一层是它本来就是好交易：房地产表现差，你可以赚钱。

turns.en: But I don't think people understood at the time was it was also a huge macro trade. So if you got it right, it was a hedge on your overall portfolio.
turns.zh: 但当时人们未必理解的是，它同时也是一笔巨大的宏观交易。你做对了，它就是你整个组合的对冲。

turns.en: The benefits of being short subprime were extraordinary at the time. The other thing is I think timing really mattered. We did subprime and it really worked well for us.
turns.zh: 当时做空次贷的收益极为惊人。另一点是，时机真的重要。我们做了次贷，对我们非常奏效。

turns.en: Our predecessors in the trade, meaning others in the industry who tried it earlier, did not do so well and some got shut down because they were too early.
turns.zh: 行业里的先行者——更早动手的那批人——做得并不好，有几个干脆被关门了，因为他们来得太早。

turns.en: Read Michael Lewis's Big Short and it's all in there and I think people don't understand the role of luck is huge and I think we in the industry and society at large celebrate as skill what really is luck often, not always and when you're lucky, you can be lucky and come across like a genius and the mistake we make as investors is to assume it was skill and not luck or not correctly or sufficiently adjusting for the fact that there's a lot
turns.zh: 去读读 Michael Lewis 的《The Big Short》，里面全都写了。我觉得人们不理解运气的角色有多大。我们这个行业和社会整体上，常常把其实是运气的东西当作能力来歌颂。当你幸运时，你可以表现得像个天才。我们作为投资者犯的错，就是把它当成能力而非运气——没有正确、充分地认识到这里面有大量的——

turns.en: of luck in this business and in investing and that's really hard to sort out. So subprime is a great example of trying to parse that out. I think a lot about the question of luck and skill and when you're investing in managers, things change inside the organizations.
turns.zh: ——运气，这真的很难厘清。所以次贷是试图拆分运气与能力的好例子。——关于运气和能力的问题我想得很多。当你投资管理人时，组织内部是会变的。

turns.en: I remember leaving business school and going to work for a manager that Yale had money with and so my prior training taught me that anybody Yale had money with was a superstar and it was a great story.
turns.zh: 我记得我离开商学院后，去给一家耶鲁投过资的管理人打工。我此前的训练让我以为，凡耶鲁投钱的都是超级明星，故事很美好。

turns.en: It was a small leverage buyout shop and I went there the first day. I was the first associate they'd ever hired and there were four or five partners and the first week one or two of the partners were in the office and the other guys weren't and then the next week there was a different guy in the office and the third week the other guys were in the office and it took me till the fourth week to realize that that was happening
turns.zh: 那是家小型杠杆收购公司。我第一天上班，是他们有史以来招的第一个 associate，上面有四五位合伙人。第一周一两位合伙人来办公室，其他人不在；第二周换另一位在；第三周又是另外几位。到第四周我才反应过来怎么回事。

turns.en: because the guys hated each other. And then my big lesson was wow people at Yale had no idea this was going on and they had entrusted their money with them.
turns.zh: 他们彼此憎恨。我最大的感触是：哇，耶鲁根本不知道这里在发生什么，却把钱托付给了他们。

turns.en: How do you, over time when you have a relationship with a manager, their life circumstances change in this business, their wealth changes, how do you stay in touch with them enough to detect if what was let's say skill or luck turns into something else because the person changes or their temperament changes or their motivation changes?
turns.zh: 当你和管理人有长期关系时，他们的人生境况在变，财富也在变，你怎么和他们保持足够接触，去发现当初是能力还是运气的那些东西变成了别的——因为人变了、性情变了、动机变了？

turns.en: Again a great question. I think the way we think about it is first the investing with a manager is it's only the starting point for the relationship that it's really about partnership that you want to give folks money that you can be in constant dialogue with and learn from and hopefully you can be of help to them as well.
turns.zh: 又一个好问题。我想我们的思路是：投给一位管理人只是关系的起点，真正重要的是合伙关系。你想把钱交给那些可以持续对话、互相学习的人，而且希望你对他们也会有所帮助。

turns.en: Those are the best. So when you have a real relationship with a firm where you're always talking about various things they get to know you pretty well but you get to know them pretty well.
turns.zh: 那才是最好的状态。当你和一家公司有真正的关系，什么都聊，他们相当了解你，你也相当了解他们。

turns.en: And I think when you have that kind of relationship it's a lot easier to get a sense for what is the cadence of the firm, how is it changing, you can look at what they own, you just get it, you can better interpret the things that you're seeing in their portfolios as to how they got into the portfolio in the first place and who might be driving decisions.
turns.zh: 有了那种关系，就更容易感知公司的节奏、它在怎么变。你可以看他们持有什么，你能更好地解读他们组合里的现象：当初是怎么进的、现在可能谁在做决策。

turns.en: And I think that's helpful if nothing's perfect in this world. But I think that's sort of absolutely one way to think about it. There's a lot of talk today about fees across active management.
turns.zh: 我觉得这很有帮助——虽然世界上没有完美的东西。我想这至少是思路之一。——现在关于主动管理的费用，有很多讨论。

turns.en: How have you thought about it differently in your relationships with your managers if you have in the last couple of years than before that and what if anything are you doing differently?
turns.zh: 过去几年，你和你的管理人相处时，对费用的思考有没有不一样？你有没有做任何不同的事？

turns.en: So look I think the first thing to say about fees is we always think of the returns we're getting from our managers net of fees very simply.
turns.zh: 关于费用，我想先说的是：我们永远简单地把管理人给我们的回报按费后来衡量。

turns.en: If they can generate great returns net of fees so be it and if they can't that's a problem. And so that's the starting point. All else equal obviously we would prefer lower fees if all else is equal.
turns.zh: 如果费后他们还能创造很棒的回报，那就好；如果不能，那就是问题。这是起点。其他条件相同时，我们当然希望更低费用。

turns.en: The question is all else equal I think and the answer often is no. For the kinds of skill we're looking for you need talent and talent is expensive.
turns.zh: 问题就在其他条件相同——而答案往往不是。我们要寻找的那类能力需要人才，人才是昂贵的。

turns.en: So the idea that you can generate high alpha for low fees I think is a complete misnomer very hard to do. I think I can see how there are certain firms where the fee levels are needed to be high or maybe are egregiously high and it wipes out the value they can add and you just don't need to invest with them.
turns.zh: 所以低费用高 alpha 这个说法，我觉得是完全的误称，非常难做到。我能理解有些公司费用必须很高，或者高得离谱、抹平了它们能创造的价值——那就不投，很简单。

turns.en: That's very easy. But when you find true talent you've got to pay them and I think you're kidding yourself if you think you can get the combination of extraordinary performance and talent for very low fees.
turns.zh: 那很容易。但当你找到真正的人才，你就得付钱。如果你以为能以很低费用拿到超群业绩加顶尖人才的组合，那是自欺欺人。

turns.en: I don't see how that works. What are you concerned most about in the capital markets today? It's crowded. I think it's crowded. A lot of money chasing seems like fewer opportunities.
turns.zh: 我看不到那怎么可能成立。——当下资本市场你最担心什么？——拥挤。我觉得很拥挤。大量的钱在追逐看似更少的机会。

turns.en: You need to go further and further afield to find things. So for example as I said earlier we're looking to give folks more specialized mandates in areas but you have to go further afield to find those.
turns.zh: 你得越走越远才能找到东西。比如我之前说的，我们想给人更专门的委托，但那些机会越来越偏。

turns.en: When you do go further afield for those do you find you tend to gravitate to smaller cap and less liquid necessarily? I think a lot of the time it is that because that's where it's harder to put money to work but you also find there are smaller firms, they're not well known.
turns.zh: 当你真的走得更远时，你会不会自然走向更小市值、更非流动？——很多时候是的，因为那里钱更难投出去。但你也会发现有些小公司，不为人知。

turns.en: You need to better understand the people. You're often one of a very small number of investors with that firm and you just can't take, there's no such thing as safety numbers where you can hope and rely on other people doing the work.
turns.zh: 你需要更好地理解人。你常常只是他们极少数投资人中的一个。没有人多安全这回事，不能寄希望于别人替你做好功课。

turns.en: You have to absolutely do your own work and have confidence that you can identify these things. So I think it's crowded. I do worry a lot about the political system today.
turns.zh: 你必须完全自己做功课，并且相信自己能识别这些东西。所以我觉得确实拥挤。我也很担心今天的政治体系。

turns.en: I do worry about protectionism. I do worry about the freedom of the press. Things that go well beyond investing but I think these things all hang together.
turns.zh: 我担心保护主义，担心新闻自由。这些远远超出投资，但我认为它们全都彼此关联。

turns.en: The economy seems to be doing fine but valuations are high and so the question always is valuations are high. My sincere hope is that they're high because things are going to be great and that would be awesome.
turns.zh: 经济似乎还不错，但估值很高。估值高这个问题永远在于：我真诚的希望，它们高是因为接下来事情会很好——那会非常棒。

turns.en: But you always have to worry they may be high because there's a little more exuberance in the markets today than is justified by the fundamentals and so one has to be cautious and always be prepared for downturns but part of being prepared for a downturn is thinking about where will there be opportunities and having dry powder to put to work on those days.
turns.zh: 但你永远得担心，它们高也许只是因为今天的市场比基本面所允许的多了几分亢奋。所以必须谨慎，永远为下行做好准备。而准备下行的一部分，就是想清楚机会会在哪里，并留有干火药，在那天到来时投出去。

turns.en: You know I guess we all hope that we're going to be able to make America great again but at the same time the political, the populism, everything you mentioned, it's hard not to wake up some days and sort of be worried that the world we're looking at for the next, I don't know, 10, 20 years is so different and a lot less comfortable than the world we've been living in or maybe that we in the financial markets were a little bit blind
turns.zh: 我们都希望让美国再次伟大，但同时政治、民粹主义，还有你提到的一切——很难不让人有些天醒来时担心：未来 10 年、20 年我们要面对的世界，跟我们一直生活的世界差别太大、让人不那么安心。也许金融市场对全国其他地方一直在感受的东西，多少有点——

turns.en: to what the rest of the country was really feeling all along. How do you take that awareness and apply it certainly in your investment portfolios but also in how you think about both the business and investing and then in life?
turns.zh: ——视而不见。你如何把这种觉察运用到你的投资组合里，并进而影响你看待生意、投资乃至人生的方式？

turns.en: Look I think in life the hardest question is we all know how this could evolve. We can all see the beginnings of authoritarianism, nationalism, economic nationalism and we all know where that could lead and there I worry about, you know it may not be in my lifetime but in my kid's lifetime and I worry a lot about that.
turns.zh: 在人生层面，我觉得最难的问题是：我们都知道事情可能怎么演化。我们都能看出威权主义、民族主义、经济民族主义的端倪，也都知道那可能通向哪里。这让我担忧——也许不在我有生之年，但可能在我孩子的有生之年，我对此非常担心。

turns.en: I think for investing I think one has to take the view that good things can happen. There's certainly, I see a lot of good things that could happen.
turns.zh: 在投资层面，我认为必须相信好事可能发生。我确实看到很多可能发生的好事。

turns.en: If society has and today we have the extraordinary ability to make good things happen if we would just work together and so there's upside and we may come to our senses and things could be fantastic but I think the tail risks are high today.
turns.zh: 如果社会——我们今天拥有让好事发生的非凡能力，只要大家愿意一起干。所以有上行空间，也许我们会恢复理智，事情会非常美好。但我认为当下的尾部风险很高。

turns.en: I think one has to think about tail risk, small probability but big impact events including I would say I wouldn't you know I think whatever probability you put on having a major war in the world I think it's always been small in recent years but however small it is it's probably double that small, still small but maybe a little bigger than it was before.
turns.zh: 必须思考尾部风险：小概率、大冲击的事件，包括战争——我不知道你会给世界性大战设多少概率，过去这些年它一直很小；但无论多小，现在大概都翻倍了：还是小，但也许比之前大一点。

turns.en: It's a tail risk it's something we need to think about and just be a little more conscious of as we make investment decisions. At the end of these podcasts I always try to ask some fun closing questions.
turns.zh: 这是个尾部风险，是我们做投资决策时要想一想、多一分警觉的事。——每期播客最后，我都会试着问几个有趣的收尾问题。

turns.en: My first question, what was your favorite sports moment as a participant or an observer? I think you should know I love to play golf. I'm a golf nut and apparently you have a great short game is that right?
turns.zh: 第一个问题：作为参与者或旁观者，你最喜欢的体育瞬间是什么？我想你也知道，我酷爱高尔夫，我是个高尔夫迷。——听说你的短杆非常出色，是吗？

turns.en: I'll let others be the judge of that but every now and then I'm able to really score a lot of the time it's useless but every now and then I can really score and those have been and I've had a couple of fantastic rounds and those you never forget those are very special and last forever in your mind.
turns.zh: 这让别人来评判吧。我时不时真能打出低杆数，大多数时候很烂，但偶尔真能打好的那几轮——我有过几轮绝妙的球——那种你永远忘不了，在心里特别珍贵，能留一辈子。

turns.en: So one of those was at the Masters and that was your favorite moment? One of those was at the Masters and you can never forget playing Augusta and having a good time.
turns.zh: 其中一轮是在大师赛上。——那是你最喜欢的瞬间吗？——其中一轮是在奥古斯塔。在奥古斯塔打球、享受其中的感觉，你永远忘不了。

turns.en: How about recommending a recent book, TV show or podcast that you've enjoyed? So I love Michael Lewis's writings. I think he's someone who thinks about the world in a way that is very unique.
turns.zh: ——推荐一本你最近喜欢的书、剧或播客？——我太爱 Michael Lewis 的作品了。他思考世界的方式非常独特。

turns.en: He has a way of seeing through what's really going on and developing a framework. So I like all these books. The one I think is most profound is Moneyball.
turns.zh: 他有一种穿透表象、看到真相并建立框架的能力。他这些书我都喜欢，但我觉得最深刻的就是 Moneyball。

turns.en: I think it's not that recent but it's an example of how he wrote about applying techniques of investing to talent management and finding great players on a team and it extends to so many aspects of life.
turns.zh: 它不算很新，但它写的是如何把投资的方法用在人才管理上、如何在球队里找到伟大的球员——这套思路能延伸到生活的很多方面。

turns.en: I just love the guy. What is your favorite thing to do that is a complete waste of time? Back to golf, I love, I'm always struggling. As any golfer knows it's a struggle and putting often just doesn't work and I will go and research new putters, buy new putters and find the problem is the six inches between the ears not the putter and talk about a waste of time.
turns.zh: 我就是太喜欢这家伙了。——你做的最浪费时间的事是什么？——还是高尔夫。我总在挣扎，任何打高尔夫的人都知道这是场修行，推杆常常就是不行。于是我去研究新款推杆、买新推杆，最后发现问题在耳朵之间那六英寸，而不是推杆——这才叫浪费时间。

turns.en: That's what it is but it's great fun to always imagine. Where are you saying it's the magician and not the wand? Exactly. Exactly. What do you know today that you wish you knew ten years ago?
turns.zh: 就是这样，但幻想一下也总有乐趣。——你是说问题不在魔杖而在巫师？——正是。正是。——你现在知道什么，是希望十年前就知道的？

turns.en: Well obviously I'd like to know where markets have gone. That's always nice to know. In the ten years. There's a movie. There's a Back to the Future.
turns.zh: 显然我想知道市场会往哪里去，那总是好的。十年……有部电影，《回到未来》。

turns.en: Something like that. Exactly. Yeah. You know I think in the last ten years if you think what's happened we've had a terrible year and a bit during the financial crisis where extraordinary things happened far beyond anything we could imagine and then likewise we've had a recovery in the markets that's been unbelievable including US equities in particular.
turns.zh: 差不多就是那个感觉。是的。我想过去十年里，我们经历了金融危机中糟糕的一年多一点，发生了远超我们想象的事；同样地，我们也经历了不可思议的市场复苏，美国股市尤其如此。

turns.en: I wish I'd known then how bad it could be but also how resilient the world could be and how we've come back. So things like that but that's always in hindsight.
turns.zh: 我希望我当时就知道，情况能坏到什么程度，也希望我知道世界能有多坚韧、能反弹成什么样。诸如此类，但那永远是事后诸葛。

turns.en: It's always easier to think back what you'd like to have known. You are now 110 years old. You are sitting in your rocking chair which is your favorite passion at the time.
turns.zh: 事后想本应知道什么总是容易的。——假设你现在 110 岁，坐在摇椅上，回味你此生最热爱的事业。

turns.en: What advice would you give yourself looking back at your life today? You mean what advice would I give myself for the next phase in my life starting now?
turns.zh: 回望你的人生，你会给今天的自己什么建议？——你是问，从现在开始的下一阶段，我会给自己什么建议？——对。

turns.en: Correct. And I would say firstly I think the beauty of life is there's no such thing as being too old. I think there's no such thing as retirement.
turns.zh: 首先，我觉得人生的美妙在于：没有太老这回事。我觉得没有退休这回事。

turns.en: I think you should never retire. There's no such thing as think small. You should always think big. You should always try and have an impact and think about what can you do to have an impact.
turns.zh: 你永远不该退休。永远不要想小。永远要往大处想，总要试着去产生影响——想想你能做什么来产生影响。

turns.en: Have energy. I think basic things like the power of networking. It's critical to do anything in this world. You have to be able to network well and you can never rest on an old network.
turns.zh: 保持能量。一些最基本的东西，比如人脉的力量——在这个世界做成任何事都至关重要。你必须善于经营网络，永远不能躺在旧的人脉上。

turns.en: You have to keep refreshing, replenishing and that takes hard work. It's all about relationships. I would say those things never get old. They never stop.
turns.zh: 你必须不断刷新、不断补充，这需要下苦功。一切都是关系。我想说，这些东西永远不会过时，永远不会停。

turns.en: And those are the things that make life interesting, work life interesting and just keep doing them. You realize as you get older that life's about family, family, family.
turns.zh: 正是它们让生活有趣、让工作有趣，继续做下去就是了。你越上年纪越会意识到：生活是关于家庭的——家庭、家庭。

turns.en: Never forget that. And I think we talked about luck. Luck really matters. So if you can make your luck, you're that much better off. And it's a version of you can't win the lottery if you don't buy a lottery ticket.
turns.zh: 永远别忘了这一点。我们聊过运气——运气真的很重要。如果你能为自己制造运气，你就比别人强一大截。这就像那句不买彩票就中不了奖。

turns.en: You've got to find ways to make luck for yourself. Are you recommending buying lottery tickets or just trying to clarify that? So I think you should always be taking risks.
turns.zh: 你得想办法为自己制造运气。——所以你在推荐买彩票吗？我只是确认一下。——我觉得你的人生应该不断冒险。

turns.en: You want to manage your risks, but you want to take risks because good things happen when you take risks. Not crazy risks. I'm not saying not be prudent, but you want to take risks.
turns.zh: 你要管理风险，但也要主动承担风险，因为好事发生在冒险之时。不是疯狂的险——还是要审慎——但你得去冒险。

turns.en: If you don't take risks, taking risks is interesting. You learn it's exciting. It works if you're thoughtful about it and you always have a chance when you do that.
turns.zh: 如果你不冒险——冒险是有趣的，你能学到东西、感到兴奋。只要你思考周全，冒险是行得通的，而只要你这么做，你就永远有机会。

turns.en: Fantastic. Andre, this is so much fun. Thanks for doing this. Thanks, Ted. I appreciate it. Thanks for listening to this episode. I hope you found a nugget or two to take away and apply in your investing and your life.
turns.zh: 太棒了。André，今天真的非常开心，谢谢你来做这期节目。——谢谢你 Ted，我很感激。——感谢收听本期节目，希望你找到一两块值得带走的金子，用在你的投资和人生里。

turns.en: If you've liked what you've heard, please rate a review on iTunes or Google Play to help others find out about the show. Have a good one and see you next time.
turns.zh: 如果你喜欢听到的内容，请在 iTunes 或 Google Play 打个分、写条评论，让别人也能发现这个节目。祝你愉快，下次见。
